full_judgment:
4. The respondent No.1 herein, United Fish Export Limited represented by its Managing Director, as plaintiff, filed Money Suit No.19 of 1993 before the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Khulna impleading Sadharan Bima Corporation (the present petitioner) and others as defendants for a decree of Tk. 1,17,00,000/- (Taka one crore seventeen lacs) only and for further decree for statutory interest @ 5% above the bank rate for the period from the date of accident to the date of realization. The defendant Sadharan Bima Corporation contested that suit by filing written statement. The trial court, on consideration of the evidence adduced by both the contesting parties, and other facts and circumstances decreed that suit directing the Sadharan Bima Corporation to meet up the plaintiffs claim of insurance by the judgment and order dated 23.11.1999. Against this judgment of the trial court the plaintiff filed Miscellaneous Case No.7 of 2000 under section 114 of the Civil Procedure Code seeking review of that judgment stating, inter alia, that in that suit the plaintiff claimed interest also as provided in section 47B of the Insurance Act but the court, though decreed the suit, but omitted to make any observation regarding the plaintiffs claim of interest. In that review application the plaintiff prayed for amendment of the judgment and decree dated 23.11.1999 by allowing and awarding statutory rate of interest since filling of claim by the plaintiff. The trail court allowed that review application which was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 2000 and considering the facts and circumstances and also the legal position awarded interest @ 5% above the bank rate as claimed by the plaintiff by the, judgment and order dated 02.08.2000. 

 5. Being aggrieved by the original judgment dated 23.11.1999 passed in Money Suit No. 19 of 1993 M/s. Sadharan Bima Corporation filed the F.A. No. 345 of 2000 before the High Court Division and being aggrieved by the judgment and order dated 02.08.2000 passed in Miscellaneous. Case No. 7 of 2000 under section 114 of the Civil Procedure Code Sadharan Bima Corporation filed the F.A. No. 564 of 2000 before the High Court Division. A Division Bench of the High Court Division heard both these appeals together and by the impugned single judgment and order dated 18.03.2009 dismissed both the appeals affirming the judgment and decree of the trial court. 

 6. The case of the plaintiff of Money Suit No.19 of 1993 (the present respondent No.1), in short, was that the plaintiff was a private limited company incorporated on 31st December, 1987 and had been carrying on fish processing and exporting business since 1988 at huge expenses with the financial help of M/S. Janata Bank. That the plaintiff insured their plant and factory machineries as well as stock of frozen fishes with Sadharan Bima Corporation i.e. the defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 5. That the insurance company the defendant No. 1, after due investigation, examination and scrutiny of the stock of the fishes and the machineries agreed to cover the risk of Deterioration of Stock (DOS) for Tk. 1,15,00,000/- and for Machinery  Break Down (MBD) for Tk. 35,80,000/- In 1990, the plaintiff took DOS and MBD policies from the defendant No. 1, who after proper inspection and examination agreed to cover such policies against payment of premiums. The rate of premiums was fixed by the defendant No. 1 and those premiums were paid regularly by debiting from the account of the plaintiff. The defendant No.1 issued policies, coverage note, premiums receipts and all other necessary papers in respect of coverage of risk of DOS and MBD policies. Subsequently, the policies were renewed and before its renewal the officials of the defendant No.1 visited the factory and inspected the conditions of machineries and stock of fishes. The defendant Nos.1, 2 and 5 were satisfied with the maintenance of machineries and stocks of storages. The DOS and MBD policies were lastly renewed for the period from 07.05.1992 to 06.05.1993 and before this renewal also the experts of defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 5 inspected and examined the stocks, machineries and connected installation and having found all satisfactory renewed the insurance coverage for Tk. 1,15,00,000/- against DOS policy and for Tk. 35,80,000/- against MBD policy. The premiums against DOS and MBD policies were paid in full on 06.05.1992. That the plaintiff made a contract being contract No. GP-0024(A) on 16.04.1992 with M/s. Global Trade, an agent of M/s. NV PPLETERS VISBEDRUF INDUSTRIE ZONE BLAUWE TOREN KOL VESTRAAT 4-800 BRUGGE BELGIUM for exportation of 420 master cartons frozen shrimps and obtained invoice No. FEL/92/01 dated 23.04.1992 for, 420 master cartons frozen shrimps for an amount of US$ 63,294.06. The insurer i.e. defendant Nos. 1, 2 and.5 having satisfied about the stock of 420 master cartons frozen shrimps issued transit marine cover on 10.05.1992 for 420 master cartons frozen shrimps and the said marine cover was valid for shrimps from 10.05.1992 till midnight of 09.05.1993 unless it was exhausted earlier by declaration. The transit marine covered the risk in between the cold storage and the ships and the insured: amount was US$ 51,100.00. According to the practice and procedure, a certificate was issued by the Quality Control Department of Fisheries Department after examination of stock taking random sample certifying that the consignment of fishes was found wholesome and fit for human consumption. While everything was completed for shipment of the stock of frozen shrimps, unfortunately, there was an ammonia gas leakage inside the cold storage on 22.05.1992 wherein frozen shrimps were stored. The news of accident of ammonia gas leakage was communicated to the Insurer, Bank, Police Station, Fire Brigade and Civil Defence etc. immediately. On 23.05.1992 the plaintiff wrote letter to the insurer about incident requesting the insurer for payment of coverage under DOS and MBD policies to the plaintiff. The insurer by letter dated 24.05.1992 informed the plaintiff with respect to the appointment of M/s. Asian Surveyor Ltd. for ascertaining the damage and the compensation thereof. The insurer further requested the plaintiff' to place their claim by filling up the prescribed form of the insurer. The plaintiff complied with by placing the formal claim through prescribed form requesting the insurer for payment under DOS and MBD policies. But the insurer repudiated the claim of the plaintiff by issuing a letter dated 26.04.1993. Subsequently on 07.05.1993 the insurer refused to pay the amount of coverage both under DOS and MBD policies and thus the plaintiff was compelled to file the suit. 

 7. The defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 5 being the insurer contested the suit by filing joint written statement. The material case of these defendants was that the accident occurred due to the fault and negligence of the plaintiff and that the entire machineries were old and second-hand procured 4 and obtained from an old ship in 1988. That the insurer appointed a Surveyor to ascertain and determine the actual loss, who after investigation submitted a report on 28.05.1992. That the insurer appointed a consulting engineer Mr. M. Alauddin, an expert of Cold Storage Association also to find out the exact cause of accident and evaluate the loss during the accident, who after due investigation submitted report on 25.11.1992 wherein it was disclosed that the machineries of the factory were old and second hand procured from an old broken ship in 1988. That the plaintiff by suppressing and concealing the material facts falsely and maliciously obtained the insurance policies and as such the suit is liable to he dismissed. 

 10. The learned Judges of the High Court Division appear to have considered all these pleas of the appellant deeply and on analyses of the evidence, facts and circumstance on record, opined that these pleas of the insurer have not been proved at all by any cogent evidence. The High Court Division pointed out that the original copies of the alleged inspection report prepared by the M/s. Asian Surveyor Ltd. and also Mr. M. Alauddin even had not been produced before the court and none of the M/s. Asian Surveyor Ltd. or Mr. M. Alauddin was produced before the court to prove these reports. The High Court Division also pointed out that the insurer did not feel it necessary even to adduce any evidence to prove its defence plea that all the machineries of the factory of the insured were old. The High Court Division also opined that the defendants could not prove 5% depreciation of value of shrimps per month starting from 7th month from the storage by adducing any evidence before court and that the condition of 5% depreciation attached with the policy as special endorsement being in a separate sheet of type copy having not been authenticated by any competent authority could not be taken into consideration. The High Court Division has also opined that the plaintiff has adduced sufficient evidence including three witnesses and all necessary papers which proved its case sufficiently. The High Court Division, therefore, found the judgment and decree of the trial court legal being based on evidence and dismissed both the appeals by the impugned judgment. 

 12. Mr. Tofailur Rahman has argued mainly that in this case it was the positive case of the insurer Sadharan Bima Corporation that the accident occurred for the reason that all the machineries of the factory of the ensured company was very old and purchased second hand in 1988 and that the insured company suppressing this fact entered into insurance contract illegally and fraudulently and in the circumstances the insurer cannot be made liable to satisfy the claim of the insured for the damage. Which was caused for the own fault and also fraudulent activity of the insured company. Mr. Tofailur Rahman has submitted also that after the accident the insurer caused survey of the insured factory by two, agencies, namely, M/s. Asian Surveyor Ltd. and Mr. M. Alauddin, an expert and both of them submitted reports stating that all the machineries of the factory were very old and the reason of the accident was the decrepit condition of these very old machineries. The learned advocate for the petitioner has submitted also that both the trial court and the High Court Division has failed to appreciate this evidence adduced from the insurer company and consequently arrived at a wrong finding and decision. 

 16. Before parting with, we want to record some observations. It appears that Sadharan Bima Corporation though has made claim and statements to the effect that after the accident they caused inspection and survey of the insured factory by experts and obtained experts report, but it did not even produce the original copies of those inspection reports and did not make them exhibited in accordance with law. None of the makers of these reports also has been examined before the court to prove the contents of these reports. Admittedly, before entering into the contract for insurance with the plaintiff company the insurance company caused inspection of the insured factory by experts and thereafter being satisfied about the condition of the machineries of the insured factory they entered into the contract of insurance. Now this insurance company itself is telling that the machineries of the insured factory were old and in decrepit condition. All these facts tell that the concerned officials of the insurance company were not sincere at all, rather were callous and negligent in dealing with the whole matter from the date of entering into the contract and also in conducting the case before the court.
